chunks.text: 38-year-old male, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Yishun, Singapore.
General anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, balanced technique using sevoflurane, fentanyl, and rocuronium
Appendectomy under general anesthesia 15 years ago, no complications

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. Today we'll be discussing your upcoming laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Let's start with why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. Been having belly pains for months, especially after eating. Doctor said gallstones, so need to remove the gallbladder lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine, metoprolol, atorvastatin, omeprazole, and metformin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Correct. But I stopped the metformin two days ago, like the nurse told me. Blood sugar's been okay, just a bit peckish sometimes.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any allergies documented here, but I always like to confirm. Have you ever had any allergic reactions to medications, especially antibiotics like sulfonamides?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh! The records say no allergies, but actually... I had a bad rash once from a sulfa drug. Can't remember the name, but it was for an infection. Face and chest all red and itchy for days.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. We'll update your records to note sulfa allergy with rash. Any other reactions to medications or foods?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No other allergies, but I do get heartburn easily. That's why I take omeprazole daily.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, nothing since 8pm last night. Just a bit of water with meds this morning, but that was hours ago lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Even minor procedures?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Never had any operations before. This is my first time under general anesthesia.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. How's your overall energy and mobility? Can you walk upstairs or do daily tasks without excessive fatigue?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Mostly okay, but the gallstone pain sometimes makes me tired. Still working full-time, though. Just avoid heavy lifting.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for all that. We'll use general anesthesia with a tube in your throat, and medications to keep you comfortable and relaxed. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Will I be sleepy after? My wife is picking me up, but she's worried about driving with me drowsy.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You'll need a responsible adult to accompany you home, as the effects can last a few hours. We'll make sure she's briefed on aftercare.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] 18-gauge IV placed in right antecubital fossa

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] administered 500 mL Ringer's lactate

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] blood pressure dropped to 90/60, gave 10 mL saline bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] sevoflurane at 1.5% inhaled concentration

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] fentanyl 50 micrograms IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] heart rate increased to 110, gave 0.5 mg metoprolol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit sore, ah, but manageable. My tummy hurts a little where they made the cuts.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understandable. On a scale of 1 to 10, what would you say your pain is right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5? Not too bad, but I can feel it when I move.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we’ll keep an eye on that. Any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit of nausea, yes. Felt like I might throw up earlier, but it’s better now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Got it. We’ll give you something for that. How’s your breathing? Any discomfort in your throat or chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Throat’s a bit sore from the tube, I think. But I’m breathing fine, no trouble.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Do you remember anything from the operation itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything’s blank. Woke up here, so that’s good, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Since you have hypertension and GERD, any chest burning or high BP symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: BP’s been okay, but my throat feels a bit acidic, like usual. Not worse than before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We’ll monitor your BP and give meds for the acid. You’re doing well overall.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, doctor. Hope to go home soon.
